ActivityThread.main().what: The real entry point of every app process: it prepares the main Looper, says hello to system_server, then loops forever.

Looper.loop().what: The main thread's endless loop: take one message, run it, repeat.

handler.post { … }.what: post() wraps your code in a Message and puts it in this Handler's queue.

MessageQueue.what: When nothing is due, the queue sleeps in native code until a message arrives or a timer fires.

Binder.getCallingUid().what: Native: the UID the kernel stamped on the call. The caller can't fake it.
Binder.getCallingUid().code: 338  public static final native int getCallingUid();

ZygoteInit.main().what: Zygote's main: preload the framework, fork system_server, then wait for "fork an app" requests.

SystemServer.main().what: system_server's entry point: it starts the bootstrap services (activities, packages, power…).

ActivityTaskManagerService.startActivity.what: Where your startActivity() lands inside system_server, after crossing Binder.

onCreate().what: Your override of this method is what the main thread calls when system_server says "create".

Parcel.what: The flat byte buffer that carries arguments across processes.

drivers/android/binder.what: The Binder driver in mainline Linux (now written in Rust) stamps the sender's user ID on every transaction. Android phones run Android's own kernel branches, which may still use the older C driver.
